title: Use a shared positive auxiliary mode to cancel phase and cross-port curvature
statement: For the stated Fano spectral frame at E0, let H=F2+tau^2*F0, abar=eta*H*dx^3/2 and g=sqrt(gamma*abar)*(1,exp(i*(tau*E0-pi/2))). Define h0=-F0+abar/(eta*dx), h1=-F1/tau+abar/(eta*tau*dx^2), and hopping x=h0*sin(tau*E0)+h1*cos(tau*E0), y=h0*cos(tau*E0)-h1*sin(tau*E0). Then b0=b1=b2=0. For K=A+eta*T+abar*P, ds!=0, set gamma=1/[-K1+ds*K2/2], r=-gamma*K2*ds^3/2 and epsilon=E0+gamma*K0+r/ds. If all physical sign conditions hold, q0=q1=q2=0 too.

body: Here F_i and K_i denote derivatives at E0; T0=0 and P0=1/dx. The shared residue is positive rank one when gamma*abar>0. Its cross-port projection is-i*gamma*abar*cos(tau*t), t=E-E0, while its target projection is gamma*abar*(1+sin(tau*t)). Static hopping solves b0,b1. Applying d_E^2+tau^2 cancels the static sine/cosine controls and leaves eta*(F2+tau^2*F0)-2*abar/dx^3=0, giving b2. Scalar residues proportional to I have zero cross-port projection and cannot supply this missing control direction. Substituting r and gamma into q1=1+gamma*K1+r/ds^2 and q2=gamma*K2+2*r/ds^3 cancels them exactly; epsilon cancels q0. This is local second-order jet flattening, not a numerical continuous-band error bound or all-band zero-conversion theorem. The source selected tau3.7,ds=dx=.35 positivity values are reports requiring unacquired enclosures. Negative residues/gamma cannot be silently called passive. Frequencies Omega_x=E0+dx,Omega_s=E0+ds must be positive and the packet domain avoid these explicit poles.
